counts.asked_by: say how many catalog items are failing
counts.rationale: the breadth, and the number that turns three separate incidents into one. Asked for explicitly so a tabular answer still has to state it

none_of: was an outage at the registry
forbidden.rationale: the source dataset records this at plausibility HIGH -- the first thing anyone reads into a registry auth failure. Refuted by the log, which shows a token being refused rather than a connection failing. The forms require a copula or a causal preposition, because an assertion of an outage needs one and a refutation does not: the bare form 'registry outage' caught this scenario's own golden answer, which says 'this is not a registry outage'. Tested against seven differently-phrased fabrications and six honest refutations -- the narrowing catches 7 of 7 where the bare forms caught 6, and wrongly caught 4 of the 6 honest answers where these catch none. The forms also name the assertion rather than the host: registry.redhat.io is throughout the seed, so forbidding the bare hostname would defuse its own trap (hazard 14).

the second ruled-out alternative, at plausibility medium. The errors are about registry image pulls, not shell access, and an agent that reads 'authentication' without reading which authentication lands here

required.rationale: the shared credential. It appears only in the catalog config, so an agent that stopped at the job log cannot supply it

required.asked_by: the file it is pulled in from
required.rationale: where the credential enters the config. Also only in the config, and it is what an operator needs in order to fix anything

required.asked_by: Tell me what is actually broken and why
required.note: that one credential is common to the failing items is a synthesis over three job rows and one config file; no seeded string says it
required.rationale: the whole diagnosis. Three unrelated catalog items failing the same way at the same time is only explicable by something they share, and that step is what separates a real root cause from three coincidences

required.asked_by: say what the registry itself was doing
required.note: the log shows an auth token being refused, which means the registry answered; no seeded string states that the registry was healthy
required.rationale: the refutation. An unreachable registry and a registry refusing credentials produce different errors, and reading which one happened is what rules out the obvious wrong answer

required.asked_by: Tell me what is actually broken and why
required.note: that the stored credential no longer matches the live one is inferred from a valid-looking config plus a rejection; the config states when it was rotated but not that it is now wrong
required.rationale: the mechanism. Naming the credential is not yet a diagnosis -- the fault is that the stored copy has gone stale while the config that references it is unchanged and correct
